tagline.text: A 1756 Spanish-era fort and Marian shrine guarding Panguil Bay

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Baybay Triunfo, Ozamiz City, Misamis Occidental

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: Approx. ₱300–1,500 (per person, day visit around Ozamiz city)

children.text: Cotta Fort is a stone fort from 1756 standing on the waterfront beside Ozamiz port, declared a National Historical Landmark. You can see the fort garden with its small museum, the Cotta Marian shrine facing the sea, and a lighthouse about 9 m tall all in one stop.

The fort's official name is "Fuerte de la Concepción y del Triunfo." Locally it is shortened to "Cotta," and it is also called the Fort of Misamis or Triunfo Fort. It stands right beside the port in Barangay Baybay Triunfo, Ozamiz City, at the mouth of Panguil Bay on the northwest side of Mindanao. For travelers it is the first historic sight people name in Ozamiz, and it is described as the oldest structure in the city.

The fort exists because of pirates. Around 1754, pirate raids hit coastal towns in southern Luzon, the Visayas and Mindanao, so the Spanish government created a defensive flotilla, and the Jesuit missionary Father José Ducos became its commander. After the pirates were beaten, a stone fort was planned for the mouth of Panguil Bay, and construction began in 1756. Money for workers and materials was limited, so the work took a long time, and once built the fort also sheltered Spanish fleet ships. Misamis then grew into the most important town of northern Mindanao in the 18th and early 19th centuries, and it was the capital of the District of Misamis until the 1870s, when the seat moved to Cagayan de Oro.

The name has a story behind it. Father Ducos belonged to a society devoted to the Immaculate Conception, hence "Concepción." "Triunfo" (triumph) refers both to the lead vessel in the battles that cleared pirates from Misamis harbor and Panguil Bay and to the Triumph of the Cross, the Christian victory at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212. That is why Ozamiz is often linked with Our Lady of Triumph.

Today the fort is laid out like a single connected park. It has three areas: the Cotta shrine on the sea side, the Cotta Garden inside the fort (with a small museum), and the Plaza de los Jesuitas on the shore. It does not take long to see, so it suits a few hours while you wait for a flight or boat, or as the first stop on a half-day city tour. It was restored to its original design in 2002, and on March 13 of that year the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) declared it a National Historical Landmark.

The fort has a square plan, with one side facing Panguil Bay and the opposite side facing the city. The four corners hold the San Fernando, San José, Santiago and San Ignacio bastions. The walls are built of coral and sandstone blocks bonded with lime, so the surface is rough and shows the wear of sea wind.

Outside the south wall, facing the sea, an open-air shrine holds a bas relief of the Virgin. It is a Marian shrine designated by the archdiocese, and many pilgrims come to the Birhen sa Cotta. The original relief, about 200 years old, was smashed with a bolo in the late 1950s by a mentally ill man, and a devotee set up a plaster replica that is still venerated today.

The garden inside the walls has a small museum of artifacts from the fort and from Ozamiz city. It is not large, so it works as a quick overview of the fort's history. Check the opening hours and exhibits before you visit.
On the southeast bastion stands a concrete lighthouse about
9m
tall, built around 1917. Its focal plane is about
and it shows two red flashes every

. It is a landmark for recognizing the fort from the harbor side.

blocks.title: Gate with the Santiago Matamoros relief

children.text: The large gate added in the 2002 restoration carries a relief of Santiago Matamoros (St. James the Moor-slayer), flanked by Pillars of Hercules heraldry. The decoration borrows Spanish imperial symbols directly, which makes it a good photo spot.

In October 1942 Wendell Fertig made the fort the headquarters of the growing guerrilla resistance, then left on June 26, 1943, in the face of a large Japanese attack. Japanese troops afterward garrisoned the fort and dug foxholes in and around the walls.

The trenches dug near the walls weakened the structure, and during the magnitude 7.4 earthquake of 1955 the southwest bastion collapsed. Knowing that this quake was a major turning point in the fort's history makes the walls look different.

On July 16, 2006, the Philippine Postal Corporation issued stamps marking the fort's 250th anniversary. The date matches the Ozamiz city charter day, so locals remember the fort and the city's history together on that day.

items.title: 2–3 hour route
items.subtitle: The shrine, the garden and a lap of the walls

children.text: Take a tricycle from downtown or the port to Cotta Fort. It is close to the port and can also be reached on foot.
See the Marian relief at the seaside Cotta shrine and rest for a moment. If a service is under way, watch quietly.
Go through the main gate into Cotta Garden and look around the small museum.
Walk along the top of the walls to see the bastions, the lighthouse and the sea toward Panguil Bay.
Pass through Plaza de los Jesuitas, then return downtown for lunch.
Some stretches of the walls may have low railings, so keep hold of children.

items.title: Half-day extension
items.subtitle: From the fort to the cathedral

children.text: Start with the Cotta Fort shrine and garden.
Take a tricycle to the Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception on JP Rizal Avenue. It was designed by Leandro Locsin and is said to hold the only pipe organ in Mindanao.
Have lunch and rest at a restaurant downtown.
Finish at Bukagan Hill in Barangay Malaubang, a bell tower with four large bells.
Check the opening hours of the cathedral and Bukagan Hill locally.

There are direct flights from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) in Manila to Ozamiz Labo Airport (OZC). Wikipedia lists PAL Express and Cebu Pacific serving Manila and Cebu, so check the latest airlines and schedules when you book.
The airport is north of downtown, and you reach the city by taxi or tricycle (check the fare locally).
The airport has a known expansion plan, so facilities and routes may change.

items.title: By boat from Manila or Cebu

children.text: Boats are said to run from Ozamiz port to Manila, Cebu City and Iligan. Operators and schedules change often, so confirm when you book.
Cotta Fort is right beside the port, so you can walk there after getting off the boat.

items.title: By land from Iligan and northern Mindanao

children.text: When the Panguil Bay Bridge opened in September 2024, travel between Lanao del Norte and Misamis Occidental became much shorter. Since the opening, the boats that linked Mukas and Ozamiz are reported to have been cut back to mostly cargo and vehicles.
Buses run from Iligan to Ozamiz. Wikivoyage lists a fare of about
, but that is old information, so confirm it locally.
Bus routes and transfer arrangements may have changed after the bridge opened, so check directly at the terminal.
Tricycles are the main transport in Ozamiz. Wikivoyage says about
anywhere in town, but that is old information, so ask the current fare before you board.
From a hotel near the port you can also walk to Cotta Fort.

Cotta Fort is mostly outdoors, so the drier months make it easier to walk the walls and the shoreline. I could not confirm monthly rainfall, so decide after checking the weather forecast before your trip.

Known events are the Sinulog Festival on the fourth Sunday of January (a pilgrimage with the Santo Niño image from Cebu), the Perangat Ozamiz Festival on the July 16 city charter day, and the Feast of the Immaculate Conception on December 8. These days draw crowds, so plan early.

Lodging is concentrated downtown along JP Rizal Avenue and near the port. Wikivoyage lists budget hotels and pensions at roughly ₱225–725, but the list is old, so confirm current prices and whether they are still open when you book. A hotel on the port side near the fort is also convenient for an early boat or flight.

Choose a restaurant downtown. Wikivoyage names places such as Chicken Ati-atihan, Shanghai Boy and Carmela's Restaurant, but confirm that they are still open and check prices locally. Downtown shops are said to open around 10 a.m. and close around 8 p.m.
The
National Historical Commission register
lists Cotta Fort as a National Historical Landmark in Ozamiz. Check access to the outdoor Cotta Shrine and the garden and museum inside the walls separately before visiting.
Visit the seaside shrine quietly if prayers are taking place. One
Ozamiz visitor guide
gives about
for the walled fort, while another lists
. Ask the ticket desk about current admission and exhibit access separately.
There is little shade on the walls and bastions, so bring a hat and water.
Ask the tricycle fare before you ride, and carry plenty of small change.
The Panguil Bay Bridge opening changed transport, so check the latest bus and van information for trips toward Iligan and Tangub.
On the Ozamiz charter day (July 16), the fourth Sunday of January and December 8, downtown lodging and transport can get crowded.
Much of the fare, hours and transport information is old, so always re-confirm it locally.
The top of the walls is an old stone structure and may be slippery or have low railings.
During pilgrimage events it is crowded and pickpockets may be about, so keep your belongings in front of you.
Parts of the site may close for works or events.
Boat and flight routes change often, so confirm your last connection in advance.

blocks.title: Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception

children.text: Heading toward downtown from the fort, the cathedral is on JP Rizal Avenue. It was designed by Leandro Locsin and is said to hold the only pipe organ in Mindanao (completed in 1967). It is a short tricycle ride.
Four large bells hang on a hill in Barangay Malaubang. Wikivoyage explains that they were too heavy for the cathedral, so they were placed here.
Known as a roughly 12-hectare ornamental plant farm and resort in Barangay Banadero. Check locally whether it is open.
A waterfall about
52km
from Ozamiz, as Wikipedia describes it. It is on the Iligan side rather than in the same area, so it may be hard to fit into a day plan.
